title: The Fast train to the coast
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：fast　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fast 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1984 the elder wrote of ① a fast train to the coast in the memoir, and everybody in the village said at once that it was ② faster than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the elder, who never explained anything, had done it with great care and gone home; it was the fast ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the fastest train to the coast anybody in the village had ever seen, or so the memoir for November 1978 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too fast to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the youth who had come to help; the fast ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the staff at the far gate, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a fast clock in the kitchen, and said that no youth in his right mind would call it ⑥ as fast as the clock in the kitchen they had once had in the old village. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was fast or not, and he said so.

By 1991 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the memoir. What the line asked for was ⑦ something fast, and nothing besides. The youth from the next village called the whole plan ⑧ quite fast; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the memoir kept the names of the fast ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1994, on the same day, she wrote of another fast train to the coast in the same memoir, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ faster than anybody had expected. ⑩ The fastest clock in the kitchen in the whole village, she said in 1996, was the one she could never quite name; the fast ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 快（前置定语 a fast train to the coast：1984 年长者在回忆录里记下的那件快的车）
B. adj. 快／走得快（比较级 faster than：文中两处，一处比去海边的快车，一处比预想）
C. adj. 快／走得快（最高级 the fastest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 快（表语 too fast to do：母亲觉得它太快，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 走得快（前置定语 a fast clock in the kitchen：叔叔把整件事称作一桩走得快的钟）
F. adj. 走得快（同级比较 as fast as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩厨房里走得快的钟相比）
G. adj. 走得快（后置定语 something fast：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 走得快（受程度副词修饰 quite fast：那位后生的评价）

items.q: a fast train to the coast
the fastest train to the coast anybody
a fast clock in the kitchen
The fastest clock in the kitchen in

answers.why: fast 意为“快”，1984 年长者在回忆录里记下的是“一件快的车”，此处作前置定语 a fast train to the coast。
fast 意为“快”，此处用比较级 faster than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
fast 意为“快”，回忆录上 十一月 那行字说它是村子里最快的一件，故用最高级 the fastest train to the coast。
fast 意为“快”，母亲认为这件东西“太快了，谁也用不上”，too fast to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
fast 意为“走得快”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩走得快的钟”，此处作前置定语 a fast clock in the kitchen。
fast 意为“走得快”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩厨房里走得快的钟一样走得快”，同级比较用 as fast as。
fast 意为“走得快”，回忆录上那半行字要的是“走得快的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something fast。
fast 意为“走得快”，邻村子来的那位后生认为这套计划“相当走得快”，quite 修饰原级 fast。
fast 意为“走得快”，1994 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要走得快”，故用比较级 faster than。
fast 意为“走得快”，母亲 1996 年说的是“整个村子里最走得快的那一桩”，故用最高级 the fastest clock in the kitchen。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1984 年，长者在回忆录里记下了一件快的车。（a fast train to the coast）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更快。（faster than …）
母亲觉得它太快，谁也用不上。（too fast to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩走得快的钟。（a fast clock in the kitchen）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩厨房里走得快的钟一样走得快。（as fast as …）
到了 1991 年，回忆录上只剩半行字：要的是一件走得快的东西。（something fast）
answers: In 1984 the elder wrote of a fast train to the coast in the memoir.
Everybody said it was faster than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too fast to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a fast clock in the kitchen.
He said nobody would call it as fast as the clock in the kitchen they had once had.
By 1991 the memoir asked for nothing but something fast.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 fast 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1984 the elder wrote of a fast train to the coast in the memoir, and nobody forgot it.
It was the fastest train to the coast in the village, or so the memoir says.
My mother thought it too fast to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a fast clock in the kitchen, and nobody argued with him.
The youth from the next village called the plan quite fast, and everybody laughed.
The fast ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
